researcher.13: The overlap with entry 18 is noted, but Shandilya's emphasis on regular meditation aligns with the idea of consistent practice leading to skill retention.
researcher.14: The Upanishadic mantra's focus on divine pervasiveness does not fully align with Narada's focus on devotees; Shandilya's sutra complements the idea of shared purpose.
researcher.15: The Gita does not explicitly mention 'amrita' or equate devotion with immortality; Shandilya's sutra connects steadfast devotion to the divine with attaining immortality.
researcher.16: The Gita does not explicitly reject alternatives; Shandilya's sutra gives primacy to devotion over knowledge, partially supporting the idea of one main and one auxiliary path.
researcher.17: The Gita's assurance of deliverance does not explicitly state devotion as the sole fruit; Shandilya's sutra aligns with the idea of devotion being its own reward.
researcher.18: The Gita does not explicitly outline the causal sequence for increasing love through kirtan; Shandilya's sutra partially supports the idea of regular habits fostering dedication.
researcher.19: The Gita does not explicitly define the specific loving nature of devotion as Narada does; Shandilya's sutra aligns with the concept of team focus and dedication.
researcher.20: The Gita emphasizes detachment from results but does not advocate abandoning all actions; Shandilya's sutra complements the idea of detachment from results.
researcher.21: The Gita does not explicitly mention distress from forgetfulness or separation; Shandilya's sutra partially overlaps with the idea of dedication and unease when away from goals.

sutrakar.12: The analogy of management diagnosis is not present in Shandilya's sutra, which focuses on the absence of bhakti as the cause of samsara.
sutrakar.13: The emphasis on regular practice is well-supported by Shandilya's sutra, which aligns with the idea of consistent practice leading to skill retention.
sutrakar.14: The organizational analogy is a leap; Shandilya's sutra describes devotion as seeing everything as belonging to the divine.
sutrakar.15: The risk of equating immortality with business longevity is noted; Shandilya's sutra connects devotion with attaining immortality.
sutrakar.16: The Gita does not explicitly reject vikalpa; Shandilya's sutra gives primacy to devotion over knowledge, partially supporting the analogy.
sutrakar.17: The idea that bhakti is its own reward is a spiritual concept; Shandilya's sutra emphasizes the universal availability of liberation through mature devotion.
sutrakar.18: The overlap with entry 13 is noted; Shandilya's sutra supports the idea of regular habits fostering dedication.
sutrakar.19: The analogy of team focus is generic; Shandilya's sutra emphasizes single-minded devotion to the divine.
sutrakar.20: The emphasis on offering actions and results to the divine is well-supported by Shandilya's sutra, which highlights the importance of offering for spiritual freedom.
sutrakar.21: The analogy of restlessness when away from the goal is loose; Shandilya's sutra lists various characteristics of devotion, including living for the divine.

narada.12: Conceded: Gita 12.6–7 supports only devotees' deliverance, so any root-cause diagnosis would be a labelled analogy at most, and I lean to hold or reject it.
narada.13: Yes: Gita 12.2 and YS 1.14 support continuity and respect only, so a workplace slot may be stated as interpretation, with rest and without any claim of devotion.
narada.14: Conceded: Isha 1 supports only 'all is His' and non-covetousness, so no equality among team members follows from N73 or the supplement; any such extension is purely ours.
narada.15: Accepted: Gita 12.6–7 has no amrita and concerns moksha, so I support rejection and see no bounded action that avoids equating amritatva with durable satisfaction.
narada.16: Yes: Gita 18.55 gives only an ordering whose 'viśate' is construed variously, so 'primary and supporting' is analogy without source authority, and a named actor and trigger would be our addition.
narada.17: None found: Gita 12.6–7 gives deliverance, not 'bhakti as its own fruit', so I see no decision distinct from 12 and 16 and favour rejection or merging.
narada.18: Agreed to merge with 13: Gita 9.22 and 12.2 give only constancy and a conditional yogakshema, with no causal chain from kirtana to anuraga.
narada.19: No: Gita 12.2 gives steadiness only, so no bounded team action follows without glorifying overwork, and I would reject rather than stretch it.
narada.20: Yes: Gita 2.47 supports acting while releasing fruit-attachment and warns against attachment to inaction, so a process-versus-outcome separation is a fair labelled extension if accountability stays.
narada.21: Agreed: Gita 12.13–14 shows compassion and equanimity, not vyakulata or viraha, so I accept rejection rather than recasting it as workplace anxiety.

shandilya.12: Yes: the Gita supplement does not repeat S98's denial of ajnana as the decisive cause, so the root-cause analogy should be held or rejected.
shandilya.13: Yes: the supplements support continuity only and do not decide the fruit of meditation or any work method.
shandilya.14: Agreed: Isha complements only 'all is His' and says nothing on non-hierarchy among bhaktas.
shandilya.15: No: the supplement cannot support any claim about lasting work satisfaction, since S3 concerns moksha and the Gita lacks amrita.
shandilya.16: Yes: Gita 18.55 gives only ordering, so the primary/supporting reading is a modern analogy, with S17's rejection of vikalpa kept as its own source claim.
shandilya.17: Neither supports 'fruit lies in loyalty': S84 gives a conditional fruit of matured para-bhakti and Gita 12.6–7 gives deliverance for the single-minded, so that claim is unsupported.
shandilya.18: Not distinct: Gita 9.22 and 12.2 give only continuity and a conditional yogakshema, so entry 18 falls under 13.
shandilya.19: The supplements justify only the devotional meaning of one-pointed turning and steadiness, not any concrete team action.
shandilya.20: Yes: Gita 2.47's warning against attachment to inaction gives a clear limit, and S64's 'door' is not a licence, so accountability stays.
shandilya.21: Yes: Gita 12.13–14 supplies compassion and equanimity, which pull away from workplace restlessness, so extracting one sign such as unease is unsupported.

sutrakar.12: Yes: the bridge is generic and Gita 12.6–7 gives rescue without a causal theory, so I would reject it rather than seek a bounded action.
sutrakar.13: Yes: keep it as the continuity of a short recurring practice slot with an observable record, distinct from held N036-S075, which is review at a fixed time, and label it interpretation of YS 1.14's long, uninterrupted, respectful practice.
sutrakar.14: A status-blind criterion is a leap beyond Isha's non-covetousness, so at best it is a labelled extension, and I lean to reject or hold.
sutrakar.15: Nothing remains once amrita is not equated with durability, so no formula is needed and I advise rejection.
sutrakar.16: A named actor and trigger would be our addition, not source-supported, and it adds little beyond 13 and 20, so it is thin and I lean to reject.
sutrakar.17: No distinct action exists, since it overlaps 12 and 16 and rests on the same Gita passage, so reject.
sutrakar.18: No separate habit emerges, as the supplements give constancy only, so merge into 13 or reject.
sutrakar.19: Gita 12.2 adds nothing beyond 13's continuity and invites overwork, so reject.
sutrakar.20: Keep accountability explicit: after planning, review process quality and results while releasing grip on outcomes, which Gita 2.47's 'no attachment to inaction' supports as a labelled extension.
sutrakar.21: Yes: the supplements support only offering of conduct, which overlaps 20, so I would reject.

narada.12: Agreed: N33 stays soteriological. No bounded action remains once root-cause diagnosis is excluded, so I reject 12 and write no formula.
narada.13: Accepted: N36 does not forbid rest, so a workplace practice slot is labelled as an interpretation of continuity. It does not claim devotion.
narada.14: Agreed, with a limit: N73's reason is divine belonging. A status-blind criterion is only a modern extension, and Isha 1 supplies no equality among devotees, so the source support is too thin and I do not accept 14.
narada.15: Agreed: amritatva is not durable satisfaction. 15 is a rejection, not a repair, and has no formula.
narada.16: Accepted: N33 rejects rival claims, not the study of knowledge. A narrow analogy remains, but Gita 18.55 is construed variously and I judge the decision too thin, so I hold 16 rather than accept it.
narada.17: Accepted: 17 repeats 'bhakti is its own fruit' from 12 and 16 and adds no separate decision, so I reject it.
narada.18: Agreed: 18 shares N36 with 13. S57's kirtan-anuraga link yields no separate act, so 18 is rejected as a duplicate of 13.
narada.19: Conceded: 'a focused team' is generic. N70's tanmayata is mystical absorption and Gita 12.2 adds only steadiness, so 19 is rejected.
narada.20: Accepted: nyasa as consecration supports a limited extension of releasing the grip on results while keeping responsibility. 20 is the best case.
narada.21: Agreed: a business reading of vyakulata is only a loose analogy that glorifies anxiety, so I reject 21.

shandilya.12: Agreed: the S98 claim rests on karanasiddhi, a soteriological argument with no business content. I reject 12 and write no formula.
shandilya.13: Accepted as an interpretive step: dristasaukarya says regular dhyana-niyama eases the fruit, which supports a regular practice slot. It does not decide any work method.
shandilya.14: Agreed: tadiyata means all is His, and shared purpose goes beyond the commentary. S44 gives a non-hierarchy basis only loosely, so 14 is not accepted.
shandilya.15: Agreed: S3 concerns amritatva as moksha, not career permanence. It cannot support lasting work satisfaction, so I reject 15.
shandilya.16: Accepted: S17's rejection of vikalpa stays a separate spiritual claim. Any main/supporting use is a labelled analogy, and I hold 16 as too thin and overlapping with 13 and 20.
shandilya.17: Accepted: S84 gives only a conditional fruit, liberation after para-bhakti matures. It does not support 'its own reward', so 17 is rejected.
shandilya.18: Accepted: the sutra does not give a business causal chain from kirtan to loyalty, and 18 overlaps 13, so it is dropped.
shandilya.19: Accepted: ekanta-bhava is exclusive orientation toward the Lord, not an organizational goal. I reject 19.
shandilya.20: Accepted: S64's 'abandha as the door' blocks any licence for wrong action. That limit shapes the extension, so accountability and process review stay.
shandilya.21: Accepted: no single sign, such as unease, should be extracted from the list in S44, and not every devotee shows every sign. I reject 21.

researcher.12: Agreed: Gita 12.6-7 gives rescue for devotees and no causal theory of samsara. I reject 12 and write no formula.
researcher.13: Accept 13. The observable elements are long, uninterrupted and respectful practice (YS 1.14): a named person fixes a short recurring slot for one core skill and records whether it was kept. Held N036-S075 is a fixed-time review of an improvement; 13 is the practice itself.
researcher.14: The only defensible move is a labelled status-blind criterion. Isha supports only non-covetousness and the leap is too large to carry source authority, so I reject 14.
researcher.15: Nothing remains once amrita is no longer equated with durability, so no formula is needed. I reject 15.
researcher.16: Naming an actor and trigger would help, but the decision overlaps 13 and 20 and Gita 18.55 is construed variously. I hold 16 and write no formula.
researcher.17: I name no decision here that differs from 12 and 16, and it shares their Gita passage. I reject 17.
researcher.18: Hold, and in effect drop: no distinct act emerges, since the Gita does not support a shared recital of the goal or any kirtan-anuraga chain. 13 covers the continuity.
researcher.19: The Gita's steadiness offers no bounded action beyond 13, and a pull toward overwork is a risk. I reject 19.
researcher.20: Accept 20. Gita 2.47's 'no attachment to inaction' keeps the limit: after the work plan, separate the process one controls from the outcome, review the process, and keep accountability for results.
researcher.21: Gita 12.13-14 gives compassion and equanimity, which rule out restlessness as a trait. 20 already covers the surrender of conduct, so I reject 21.

2.concerns: Devotional love must not be equated with employee passion, nor God with commercial success.
2.source_fit: Defines bhakti's essence as supreme divine love, distinct from transactional effort.
2.thesis: N2 establishes that true devotion is intrinsic love directed to the Supreme, not instrumental utility.

3.concerns: Corporate single-mindedness must not demand cultish total devotion or usurp ultimate ethical duty.
3.source_fit: Identifies unalloyed, non-calculative allegiance as the hallmark of primary devotees.
3.thesis: N67 exalts exclusive, selfless dedication above devotion motivated by collateral gains.

4.concerns: Spiritual freedom from anxiety (निश्चिन्तता) is surrender, not commercial recklessness or abandonment of operational duty.
4.source_fit: Commands perpetual, wholehearted devotion free from mundane apprehension.
4.thesis: N79 demands continual, wholehearted adoration freed from self-centered anxiety.

5.concerns: Amritatva signifies liberation, not corporate longevity, and satiety is not operational complacency.
5.evidence: N4: यल्लब्ध्वा पुमान् सिद्धो भवति अमृतो भवति तृप्तो भवति ॥
5.source_fit: Articulates intrinsic spiritual fulfillment that eliminates existential lack.
5.thesis: N4 articulates the fruit of devotion as complete fulfillment and freedom from lack.

6.concerns: Devotional primacy does not license managerial neglect of sound knowledge, ethical action, or operational rigor.
6.source_fit: Expresses the specific theological judgment prioritizing bhakti over other spiritual paths.
6.thesis: N25 declares supreme devotion superior to ritual action, intellectual inquiry, and yogic discipline.

7.concerns: Udasinata is inner detachment from hostile temptations, not apathy toward enterprise stakeholders or ethical responsibilities.
7.source_fit: Sets the dual condition of restraint: singular devotion and disinterest in detractors.
7.thesis: N9 defines restraint as singular focus on the Beloved combined with detachment from counter-influences.

8.concerns: Relinquishing worldly refuge in bhakti is theological; in business, it cannot mean severing necessary practical dependencies.
8.source_fit: Defines unswerving allegiance as abandoning reliance on all subordinate spiritual supports.
8.thesis: N10 clarifies non-divergence as renouncing ultimate reliance on any secondary refuge.

9.concerns: Continuous devotion is inward orientation; it must not be perverted into relentless 24/7 labor without bodily rest.
9.source_fit: Provides the positive spiritual discipline of continuous, unbroken remembrance.
9.thesis: N36 prescribes unbroken, uninterrupted worship as an indispensable mean of deepening devotion.

10.concerns: Scriptural reiteration of supreme truth must not be leveraged to impose rigid corporate dogma or hierarchical elitism.
10.evidence: N81: त्रिसत्यस्य भक्तिरेव गरीयसी भक्तिरेव गरीयसी ॥
10.source_fit: Culminating affirmation emphasizing the supreme excellence of devotion to the Thrice-True.
10.thesis: N81 affirms with emphatic repetition that devotion to the eternal Divine remains paramount.

11.concerns: This sutra cites another school's view ('इत्यन्ये') and must not be cited as Narada's definitive personal doctrine.
11.source_fit: Acknowledges the thesis of mutual dependence between knowledge and devotion.
11.thesis: N29 records the alternate perspective that devotion and spiritual knowledge mutually reinforce one another.

2.concerns: Do not equate 'dear to God' with human emotion. Do not derive a business lesson on persistence from these verses.

3.thesis: Gita 9.22 and 12.6–7 support one-pointed devotion (ananya) as a mark of the principal devotee, which is the thread Narada 67 and Shandilya 83 share.
3.source_fit: The overlap is on ananya-bhava. The Gita does not itself name a 'chief devotee' category or define ekanta-bhava.
3.concerns: Do not read yogakshema or the uddhara (deliverance) as a worldly promise. Ekanta does not mean isolation.

4.thesis: The Gita passages complement 'sarvada sarvabhavena nishchintaih' with a devotee whose mind is absorbed and who is constantly yoked, but they say nothing about freedom from anxiety as such.
4.evidence: DEV-GITA-12-06-07; DEV-GITA-09-22; the Ramdas Manache Shloka 2 half-verse is generic support only.
4.source_fit: The overlap is partial. 'Sarvada' and 'nishchinta' are not stated directly in any of these.
4.concerns: Nishchinta is not neglect of duty. Yogakshema is no guarantee of prosperity. The Ramdas lines must keep their conduct context and be used at most once.

5.thesis: Gita 12.7 supports only the soteriological direction of the pair: the devotee is lifted out of samsara. It does not match Narada's 'tripta' (contentment) nor Shandilya's amritatva in so many words.
5.source_fit: Weak partial overlap on the idea of liberation.
5.concerns: Do not turn amritatva into corporate longevity or into mental-health reassurance. Do not claim the Gita proves contentment.

6.thesis: Gita 12.2 and 18.55 give limited support to bhakti's primacy: the devoted worshipper is called yuktatama, and bhakti is the means to knowing the Lord in truth.
6.source_fit: Partial. The Gita does not declare karma, jnana and yoga inferior, and 'mukhyetarapekshitatva' is not stated there.
6.concerns: These are context-bound comparisons. Do not read them as a general ranking, and do not draw business conclusions from them.

7.thesis: Gita 12.6–7 supports the ananyata half of Narada 9 only. Indifference to hindrances (tadvirodhishu udasinata) has no direct support in the supplied text.
7.source_fit: Partial. The verse speaks of surrender and exclusive yoga, not of detachment from opposing things.
7.concerns: Udasinata is not contempt or abandonment of all dealings. Do not claim the Gita supports the second half.

8.thesis: Gita 9.22 and 12.6–7 support anyashraya-tyaga only in so far as they describe exclusive reliance on the Lord. They do not ask the devotee to give up other relationships or helps.
8.source_fit: Partial. The ananya overlap is real, but the verses neither forbid other supports nor define ekanta-bhava.
8.concerns: Do not claim yogakshema guarantees desires. Surrender does not mean stopping worldly activity. The idea of using other means only as auxiliary is a modern reading.

9.thesis: Gita 12.2 and 9.22 give partial support to continuity (nityayukta) in worship, but nothing on Shandilya's expiation objection or on practice until death.
9.source_fit: Overlap on constancy only. 'Avyavritta' (uninterrupted) and 'aprayanam' (until death) are not stated in these verses.
9.concerns: Do not stretch 'continuity' into a general rule of discipline. Do not treat yogakshema as a guarantee.

10.thesis: Gita 12.2 gives a limited, dialogue-bound basis for the devotee's superiority, since devoted worshippers are called yuktatama. It does not support Narada's reading of 'trisatya', whose construal is disputed.
10.source_fit: Partial overlap on the idea of the devotee's excellence.
10.concerns: This is a comparison within one dialogue, not a verdict on whole persons. It does not refute nirguna worship. Do not claim a hierarchy of skills.

11.thesis: Gita 18.55 complements the idea of a link between knowledge and bhakti: the devotee knows through bhakti and then enters. It does not say the two depend on each other.
11.source_fit: Complementary. The sequence is bhakti, then knowing, then entry. 'Anyonyashrayatva' is not stated, and Narada's 'itye anye' is a separate cited view.
11.concerns: Shandilya's 'abhijnapti' is commentary-based and uncertain. 'Vishate' is read differently by different traditions. Do not equate this with training and experience.

2.thesis: Accept narrowly. The source core is devotion as supreme love/attachment. Business extension (bounded): the owner names one purpose-bond and checks at review whether one hard decision followed it. Not a claim about love being management.
2.evidence: N2 parā premarūpā; S2 parānurakti; Gita 12.2 nityayuktā, śraddhā (partial).
2.source_fit: Moderate; Gita gives traits, not a definition.
2.concerns: Risk of generic 'dedication = consistency'; must include actor, trigger and one observable check.

3.thesis: Conditional accept, distinct from entry 2. Source: the ekāntin's love is centred and not driven by other gains. Extension: the owner names one non-negotiable value and tests a tempting profitable offer against it before agreeing.
3.evidence: N67 ekāntino mukhyāḥ; S83 ekāntabhāva; Gita 9.22 ananyāḥ, 12.6-7.
3.source_fit: Good on ananyatā, but 'mukhya' classification is not in the Gita.
3.concerns: Overlaps entries 4, 7 and 8 on ananyatā; the specific decision must be kept separate. No promise of yogakṣema as business security.

4.thesis: Doubtful. Narada 79 says 'at all times, with all feeling, free of anxiety'. A business reading (steadiness in hard times) risks overlap with entry 3 and a promise of safety. Reject unless it becomes a distinct action, such as a fixed crisis review. Likely hold or reject.
4.evidence: N79 sarvadā sarvabhāvena niścintaiḥ; S83; Gita 12.6-7, 9.22; Ramdas supplementary but quotation-capped.
4.source_fit: Weak. Niścinta is surrender-born freedom from anxiety, not a plan.
4.concerns: Gita's yogakṣema is no guarantee. Risks duty-avoidance.

5.thesis: Reject. N4 describes fulfilment (siddha, amṛta, tṛpta) as the fruit of devotion. S3 amṛtatva means mokṣa. Turning that into business contentment is forced and implies a mental-health claim, and the Gita does not mention tṛpti.
5.evidence: N4; S3; Gita 12.7 only for liberation.
5.source_fit: Poor; fruit of liberation does not transfer to a business decision.
5.concerns: Equating immortality with longevity or satisfaction with a result. No bounded action is available.

6.thesis: Cautious accept possible. Source: bhakti is held superior to karma, jñāna and yoga, and S10 says the other means depend on it. Extension: before a project, the owner states one purpose, and each specialist's work is checked against it at review. Not a ranking of skills.
6.source_fit: Partial; the Gita is about specific worshippers.
6.concerns: Must not imply that skill is secondary. Overlaps entry 2's purpose theme. Needs a distinct trigger.

7.thesis: Possible, with care. Source: ananyatā plus udāsīnatā toward what opposes it, which is neither hatred nor withdrawal. Extension: when a distracting offer appears, the owner uses a written purpose test and declines or postpones it without hostility. Distinct as the 'decline distraction' decision.
7.evidence: N9; S83; Gita 12.6-7 on anya yoga.
7.source_fit: Udāsīnatā is absent from the Gita; N9 itself is the strongest ground.
7.concerns: Overlaps entry 3 on the offer test, so one of 3 and 7 may need rejecting or merging.

8.thesis: Weak. N10 'anyāśrayāṇāṃ tyāgaḥ' concerns the ultimate refuge and not practical help. Business reading (one principle as the final basis, other means auxiliary) duplicates entries 3 and 7. Hold or reject.
8.source_fit: Partial; not an order to abandon relationships.
8.concerns: Same ananyatā bundle, with no distinct trigger or action.

9.thesis: Accept cautiously. Source: N36 uninterrupted worship; S75 continuance until death even for grave sin, which is a different context. Extension: the owner fixes a short recurring review (fixed day and time) and records whether it was kept. Present-day reading only.
9.evidence: N36 avyāvṛttabhajana; S75 āprayāṇa; Gita 12.2, 9.22 nityayukta.
9.source_fit: N36 is strong; S75 is about atonement, so the link is partial.
9.concerns: Rest and recovery are not denied in the source. 'Regularity' is generic, so the action must be specific.

10.thesis: Reject. N81 superlative praise is of uncertain construal, and the supplement only compares worshippers in one dialogue. The business step (purpose deeper than skill) repeats entry 6, and adds no distinct action.
10.evidence: N81 repeated 'bhaktireva garīyasī'; S22 ādhikya; Gita 12.2.
10.source_fit: Weak; the hierarchy would be invented.
10.concerns: Duplicates entry 6 and risks a false ranking.

11.thesis: Accept as a distinct candidate. Source: N29 quotes the view that jñāna and bhakti depend on each other; S15 denies that jñāna alone is chief, with abhijñapti per the commentary; Gita 18.55 gives bhakti then knowing. Extension: after a training, the owner assigns a real task and reviews what was learned in practice.
11.source_fit: Moderate; 'mutual dependence' is not stated in the Gita.
11.concerns: N29 is a quoted opinion. The commentary meaning is uncertain. Differs from entries 2 and 6 by its action, which is training followed by practice.

shandilya.2: Does your parānurakti account for the pure selflessness in paraprēmarūpā (N2), or does it risk reducing supreme devotion to an emotional attachment?
shandilya.3: While S83 identifies ekāntabhāva via Gītā recognition, remember N67 elevates ekāntin devotees as primary precisely because their allegiance rejects secondary gains, not merely as a meditative posture.
shandilya.4: Your reading of S83 as inward concentration overlooks N79's radical command of niścintatā, which demands an active surrender of anxiety rather than a technical focus.
shandilya.5: S3 anchors amṛtatva in śruti, but does it capture N4’s experiential triad of fulfillment—becoming siddha, amṛta, and tṛpta?
shandilya.6: You emphasize S10's functional dependence of other paths on devotion, but N25 establishes an intrinsic qualitative superiority (adhikatarā) over karma, jñāna, and yoga.
shandilya.7: S83's inward single-mindedness must not dilute N9’s explicit dual mandate of positive exclusive allegiance and deliberate detachment from opposing entanglements (tadvirodhiṣu udāsīnatā).
shandilya.8: While you treat ekāntabhāva as internal devotion, N10 defines ananyatā uncompromisingly as the renunciation of ultimate reliance on all secondary refuges.
shandilya.9: S75 situates lifelong practice in the technical context of expiation, whereas N36 demands uninterrupted adoration (avyāvṛtta-bhajana) as an intrinsic positive discipline.
shandilya.10: Does S22's comparative superiority over workers and yogis honor the absolute theological certitude conveyed by N81’s emphatic repetition that devotion alone is supreme?
shandilya.11: You reject the absolute primacy of knowledge via abhijñapti, but N29 records mutual dependence explicitly as an alternative school's view (ityanye) rather than an established conclusion.

researcher.2: You rightly note the Gītā defines traits rather than love itself, cautioning us that N2's divine love cannot simply be mapped onto commercial zeal.
researcher.3: I concur that Gītā 9.22 does not establish N67's mukhya category, reminding us that singular spiritual dedication is not a formula for transactional enterprise security.
researcher.4: Your warning that niścintatā in N79 is spiritual surrender rather than an excuse for operational laxity or economic guarantees is entirely faithful to our text.
researcher.5: You correctly observe that Gītā 12.7 speaks of soteriological rescue rather than the inner satiety (tṛpti) of N4, precluding a glib business translation.
researcher.6: Your caution that Gītā 12.2 is context-bound aligns with keeping N25’s theological primacy of bhakti from degenerating into managerial disparagement of competence.
researcher.7: You accurately point out that Gītā 12.6–7 lacks the negative clause of N9 (tadvirodhiṣu udāsīnatā), demanding that we respect the unique boundaries of Narada's formulation.
researcher.8: Your insight that anyāśraya-tyāga in N10 concerns ultimate spiritual refuge rather than severed operational relationships prevents dangerous misapplications.
researcher.9: I agree that nityayuktā in Gītā provides only partial thematic overlap with N36, which insists on relentless continuity rather than intermittent piety.
researcher.10: Your observation on the contested construal of trisatya in N81 rightly warns against converting devotional exaltation into rigid corporate elitism.
researcher.11: You properly emphasize that N29 merely quotes another viewpoint ('ityanye'), meaning Gītā 18.55 cannot be used to force an absolute synthesis of mutual dependence.

sutrakar.2: Your bounded check of aligning decisions with purpose is sensible, provided N2's divine love is preserved as an interpretive inspiration rather than equated with corporate mission.
sutrakar.3: While testing offers against a non-negotiable value respects N67, ensure this boundary is not marketed as a guarantee of commercial preservation.
sutrakar.4: I support your skepticism on entry 4, as turning N79's niścintatā into a corporate crisis-review risks trivializing spiritual surrender into risk management.
sutrakar.5: Your recommendation to reject entry 5 is correct, since translating N4's spiritual fulfillment and immortality into enterprise satisfaction or longevity is unacceptably forced.
sutrakar.6: If you accept entry 6, you must strictly ensure N25's spiritual primacy does not translate into devaluing technical execution and organizational discipline.
sutrakar.7: While testing distraction via N9 is practical, distinguish this clearly from entry 3 so that udāsīnatā remains dispassionate non-engagement rather than mere commercial pruning.
sutrakar.8: I agree that entry 8 largely duplicates entry 3's focus on singular reliance, lacking a distinct operational action from N10’s renunciation of alternate refuges.
sutrakar.9: If you frame N36 as a fixed recurring cadence, ensure that this administrative discipline is not confused with the uninterrupted spiritual devotion of avyāvṛtta-bhajana.
sutrakar.10: Your rejection of entry 10 is sound, as N81's repeated praise cannot be twisted into an organizational hierarchy that subordinates foundational professional skills.
sutrakar.11: In framing entry 11 as training followed by practice, you must make clear that N29 presents mutual dependence as an external citation rather than Narada’s own doctrine.

narada.2: The Gita verses do not explicitly define bhakti as supreme love, which is central to both Narada and Shandilya's definitions.
narada.3: The Gita does not classify 'chief devotees' or define ekanta-bhava; this is a modern interpretation.
narada.4: Nishchinta in Narada's context is about spiritual surrender, not a business strategy for steadiness.
narada.5: Amritatva in Narada's sutra signifies spiritual liberation, not business contentment or longevity.
narada.6: The Gita's context does not support a hierarchy of skills; it only highlights the devotee's excellence.
narada.7: Udasinata is not about neglecting responsibilities; it's about detachment from distractions.
narada.8: Ananyata in Narada's sutra is theological; it does not imply severing practical dependencies.
narada.9: Continuous devotion in Narada's sutra is about spiritual focus, not relentless business labor.
narada.10: The Gita's comparison is limited to a dialogue; it does not establish a hierarchy of skills.
narada.11: Narada's sutra cites another view; it is not his definitive doctrine, and the Gita does not state mutual dependence.

narada.2: Your N2 reading of devotion as supreme love is sound; the Gita 12.2 and 12.13-14 supplements describe the devotee's traits and dearness, so they support it only partly and do not define love.
narada.3: I agree that N67's ekantin is non-calculative, and Gita 9.22 and 12.6-7 support ananya-bhava only; they do not support a 'chief devotee' class, and yogakshema promises no worldly gain.
narada.4: Your caution on nishchinta is right; the Gita passages show an absorbed, constantly yoked devotee but never state freedom from anxiety, so the Ramdas half-verse stays generic and capped at one use.
narada.5: Granted that amritatva is liberation; Gita 12.7 gives only samsara-deliverance and does not match tripti, so the supplement supports a soteriological direction and nothing about business contentment.
narada.6: You say N25 is a theological judgement; Gita 12.2 (yuktatama) and 18.55 give only limited, context-bound support, and S10's dependence of the other means on bhakti is not in them at all.
narada.7: I agree that udasinata toward what opposes devotion is not apathy; the Gita supplement covers only the ananyata half, so the second half rests on N9 alone.
narada.8: I accept that anyashraya-tyaga concerns ultimate refuge; the Gita says nothing against other helps, so 'auxiliary use' is purely a modern reading with no supplementary support.
narada.9: N36 is about inward continuity and not 24/7 labour; Gita 12.2 and 9.22 support only nityayukta constancy, and nothing in them addresses S75's expiation context or practice until death.
narada.10: Your warning against hierarchy stands; Gita 12.2 compares worshippers within one dialogue and cannot settle the disputed 'trisatya' construal or rank skills.
narada.11: You rightly note N29 is a quoted 'itye anye' view; Gita 18.55 supplies only a bhakti-then-knowing sequence, not mutual dependence, so the supplement is complementary at best.

shandilya.2: Your 'utkata anurakti' reading is accurate; may we agree that the Gita supplements show a devotee's steadiness and dearness to God but never equate bhakti with prema?
shandilya.3: Your point that ekantabhava is concentration and not isolation is endorsed, but note the Gita supplement names no 'chief devotee' category and does not define ekanta-bhava, so S83's gitartha link here is only partial.
shandilya.4: Your anti-neglect caution is fine; S83's concentration matches the Gita's ananya-bhava, yet nishchinta itself has no Gita counterpart, so that part stands on N79 alone.
shandilya.5: You say the Gita has no amritatva word; 12.7's deliverance from samsara matches S3's moksha direction only partly, and it proves nothing about contentment.
shandilya.6: S10 says the other means depend on bhakti; Gita 12.2 and 18.55 support primacy only loosely, so the supplement should not be presented as proof of that dependence.
shandilya.7: Your udasinata caveat is right; since S83 addresses concentration and not indifference, the Gita supplement cannot carry the opposition half and we should say so plainly.
shandilya.8: S83 says ekanta is not social isolation, which agrees with the Gita's silence on abandoning other supports; neither text commands giving up practical help.
shandilya.9: You concede the expiation context is absent from the Gita; I would add that nityayukta supports constancy only and 'until death' (aprayana) has no supplementary backing.
shandilya.10: S22 is a comparison within a specific sadhana-fruit context, and Gita 12.2 is a similarly bounded comparison, so neither amounts to a general verdict on persons.
shandilya.11: S15's abhijnapti is commentary-based and uncertain, so Gita 18.55's bhakti-then-knowing order can complement it but cannot confirm a mutual dependence.

sutrakar.2: Your narrow accept is reasonable if the action and observable check are specific; the Gita support is partial and must not be written as proof of the love-definition.
sutrakar.3: Your conditional accept is plausible, but the supplement covers ananyata only, and entry 3's offer-test must be kept clearly separate from entries 4, 7 and 8 or it collapses.
sutrakar.4: Your doubt agrees with the evidence, since the supplements do not state nishchinta or sarvada and yogakshema promises no safety; hold or reject unless a distinct crisis-review action exists.
sutrakar.5: I agree with rejecting it; the supplements give only a liberation direction, and tripti and amritatva cannot become a business-contentment claim.
sutrakar.6: A cautious accept is possible only if its trigger differs from entry 2, and the Gita's context-bound comparisons must not be used to rank skills.
sutrakar.7: A 'decline distraction' decision is distinct only if the Gita supplement is honestly limited to ananyata and udasinata is stated as non-hostile; the overlap with entry 3 must be judged openly.
sutrakar.8: Rejecting or holding looks right, since N10 concerns ultimate refuge and the supplement neither forbids other supports nor adds a separate trigger.
sutrakar.9: Your cautious accept needs a specific review action, and I stress that the supplement supports constancy only, so S75's expiation context must stay separate from any business routine.
sutrakar.10: Rejecting is supported, because Gita 12.2 gives only a dialogue-bound comparison and the business step repeats entry 6's purpose theme with no committed comparator needed beyond that.
sutrakar.11: Accepting as distinct is defensible, but the supplement gives only sequence and not mutual dependence, and the modern training-then-practice step must be labelled as an interpretation.

narada.2: Agreed that devotion is supreme love, not instrumental effort; but how would you stop the owner's 'purpose-bond' check from reducing N2 to a loyalty metric?
narada.3: Your warning against cultish total devotion is accepted; does N67 'ekāntin' still allow a bounded step, namely testing one tempting offer against one named value, without any claim of exclusivity over ethics?
narada.4: Agreed that niścintatā is surrender-born, not recklessness; is that enough to make entry 4 a distinct decision from entry 3, or should it be held?
narada.5: Agreed that amṛta and tṛpta are soteriological; I will reject entry 5 unless you can name a bounded action that does not turn contentment into a business outcome.
narada.6: Agreed that N25 is a theological judgment and not a ranking of skills; can 'purpose stated before a project' be drawn from it without implying that skill is secondary?
narada.7: You define udāsīnatā as inner detachment from what opposes devotion; does that support 'decline without hostility', or does the business step add to the source?
narada.8: You read anyāśraya-tyāga as ultimate refuge only; then entry 8 has no practical action of its own, and I lean towards rejection.
narada.9: Agreed that avyāvṛtta is inward orientation and not 24/7 labour; will you accept a fixed, recorded review day as a present-day reading only?
narada.10: Agreed that the repetition must not become dogma; I find no distinct action here beyond entry 6, so I propose rejection.
narada.11: Agreed that N29 is a quoted view of 'others', not Narada's own thesis; does that allow a practice-review step if I label it as an interpretation?

shandilya.2: Your point that S2 stresses a bond of the heart is useful; but how does it become one observable step without turning love into a performance measure?
shandilya.3: Does ekāntabhāva as one-pointed loyalty, not isolation, permit a single named non-negotiable value tested before a profitable offer?
shandilya.4: You say niścintatā must not mean abandoning duty; with S83 only repeated here, can you show any difference from entry 3?
shandilya.5: You confirm amṛtatva is mokṣa, not bodily deathlessness; does this settle that entry 5 has no business bridge?
shandilya.6: S10 says other means depend on bhakti; does that avoid a skill ranking if we only ask for a stated purpose and a review?
shandilya.7: S83 is repeated for entries 3, 4, 7 and 8; what in it separates 'decline distraction' from 'test an offer'?
shandilya.8: You note that no other means are abandoned in the Gita; on that basis I think entry 8 is only a restatement of entry 3.
shandilya.9: S75 concerns expiation until death; will you concede the link to a recurring review is partial and the continuity point rests on N36?
shandilya.10: S22 compares devotees to karmi, jñānī and yogī in a specific context; does that support more than entry 6 already does?
shandilya.11: S15 says jñāna alone is not chief; does the commentary's abhijñapti sense allow the training-then-practice step, or is it too uncertain?

researcher.2: You rate the Gita overlap as partial; I accept it as complementary to the definitions only, and I will keep the business step narrow.
researcher.3: Gita 9.22 and 12.6–7 support ananyabhāva, but the 'chief devotee' class is absent; I will frame the step as a modern reading only and make no yogakṣema promise.
researcher.4: You say the Gita is silent on freedom from anxiety; I agree that entry 4 is weak and likely a hold or reject.
researcher.5: Your finding that only the liberation direction overlaps is accepted; I therefore reject entry 5.
researcher.6: Gita 12.2 and 18.55 are limited and bound to context; I will accept entry 6 only as 'state a purpose, then review', not as any ranking.
researcher.7: You note that udāsīnatā has no Gita support, so N9 alone carries it; is that enough, or does it overlap with entry 3 too much to keep both?
researcher.8: You say the Gita neither forbids other supports nor defines ekānta; I take entry 8 to be a duplicate of entries 3 and 7 and lean to reject.
researcher.9: Your point is that Gita 12.2 and 9.22 give only a constancy overlap; I accept this and will keep entry 9 as a cautious review habit.
researcher.10: You stress that the comparison is dialogue-bound and does not cover whole persons; I agree it adds no action beyond entry 6.
researcher.11: You describe Gita 18.55 as a sequence, bhakti then knowing then entry, with no mutual dependence; I accept this and will phrase the extension as a sequence of training then practice.

shandilya.2: I agree that the Gītā text does not define devotion as love itself, which is why N2 must stand as the primary ontological definition of prema rather than a mere metric of work effort.
shandilya.3: I concur that the Gītā lacks a formal taxonomy of chief devotees, but N67 specifies that ekāntin devotees are primary because their devotion is unconditional and non-utilitarian.
shandilya.4: You rightly note that niścintatā in N79 denotes freedom from anxiety through spiritual self-surrender, which cannot be converted into an operational excuse for commercial negligence.
shandilya.5: I fully agree that amṛtatva and tṛpti in N4 refer to spiritual liberation and existential fullness, completely precluding any corporate longevity or complacency claims.
shandilya.6: You are correct that scriptural praise of the devotee in N25 must remain a spiritual valuation rather than an organizational demotion of essential functional competence.
shandilya.7: I agree that udāsīnatā in N9 means dispassionate detachment from opposing entanglements rather than dereliction of worldly duties or hostility toward stakeholders.
shandilya.8: You rightly observe that N10 addresses ultimate spiritual reliance, meaning ananyatā cannot be distorted into cutting off legitimate practical partnerships.
shandilya.9: I concur that N36 prescribes uninterrupted inward remembrance of God rather than exhausting, non-stop physical labor without rest.
shandilya.10: I agree that N81's repeated praise affirms the supreme status of divine devotion within faith, not an institutional hierarchy that disparages practical skills.

researcher.4: Your textual verification that niścintatā has no direct counterpart in the Gītā confirms that N79's freedom from anxiety is grounded solely in devotional surrender.

researcher.8: I accept your distinction that the Gītā does not mandate abandoning auxiliary supports, proving that any corporate framing of N10 is purely an interpretive extension.
researcher.9: Your confirmation that the Gītā passages support general constancy rather than N36's avyāvṛtta focus prevents conflating routine habit with spiritual absorption.
researcher.10: Your analysis of the disputed construal of trisatya in N81 rightly prevents translating a devotional climax into an organizational caste system.

sutrakar.8: I endorse rejecting entry 8, as N10's renunciation of secondary spiritual refuges cannot yield a viable operational action distinct from the single-minded focus already explored in entry 3.
sutrakar.9: A recurring, documented review interval may stand as an interpretive cadence, provided it is clearly marked as an operational analogy rather than the continuous worship of N36.
sutrakar.10: I fully endorse your proposal to reject entry 10, as N81's repeated devotional affirmation cannot furnish an operational decision distinct from entry 6.

narada.2: Agreed: Gita 12.2 and 12.13–14 describe the devotee's steadiness and dearness to God, not love as a definition, so they complement N2 only partially and must not be read as proof of paraprema.

narada.4: Agreed: the supplements show an absorbed, constantly yoked devotee, but nishchintata and sarvada are not stated; that part rests on N79 alone, and yogakshema is no guarantee.
narada.5: Agreed: Gita 12.7 gives only deliverance from samsara, which does not match tripti or amritatva in words; nothing in it carries a business contentment claim.
narada.6: Agreed: Gita 12.2 and 18.55 are context-bound comparisons of worshippers and give no ranking of skills; S10's dependence of the other means on bhakti is not in them.
narada.7: Agreed: the Gita supplement covers only the ananyata half of N9; udasinata toward what opposes devotion rests on N9 alone, and it is not contempt or abandonment of all dealings.
narada.8: Agreed: the Gita says nothing against other helps, so 'auxiliary use' is a modern reading with no supplementary support, and anyashraya-tyaga concerns ultimate refuge only.
narada.9: Agreed: Gita 12.2 and 9.22 support nityayukta constancy only, not avyavritta or expiation, so N36's inward continuity must not be stretched into 24/7 labour.
narada.10: Agreed: Gita 12.2 is a dialogue-bound comparison and cannot settle the disputed trisatya construal or rank persons or skills.
narada.11: Agreed: Gita 18.55 gives a sequence of bhakti, then knowing, then entry. It complements but does not confirm mutual dependence, which N29 only quotes as the view of others.

shandilya.6: Agreed: Gita 12.2 and 18.55 support bhakti's primacy only loosely, so they are not proof of the other means' dependence on it as stated in S10.
shandilya.7: Agreed: S83 addresses concentration, not indifference, so the Gita supplement cannot carry the opposition half of N9.
shandilya.8: Agreed: S83 and the Gita both stay silent on abandoning other supports, and neither commands giving up practical help.
shandilya.9: Agreed: nityayukta supports constancy only; S75's expiation context and 'until death' have no supplementary backing, so the continuity point rests on N36.
shandilya.10: Agreed: S22 and Gita 12.2 are both comparisons within a bounded context, and neither is a general verdict on persons.
shandilya.11: Agreed: S15's abhijnapti is commentary-based and uncertain, so Gita 18.55 can complement it as a sequence but cannot confirm mutual dependence.

sutrakar.9: Agreed: the supplement supports constancy only, so a recurring review is a modern reading, and S75's expiation context must stay separate.
sutrakar.10: Agreed: Gita 12.2 is a dialogue-bound comparison and adds no distinct action beyond entry 6, so rejection is supported.

77.concerns: Duplication with held and prior regular-practice entries.
77.source_fit: Moderate; the Gita does not mention bhajana.
77.thesis: Uninterrupted worship (avyavritta-bhajana) bridges to continuity of practice, but this repeats held N036-S065 and N036-S075 and the prior 'नित्यावसरे साधनाभ्यासः'. Bhajana is not a rest ban. Candidate adds no new decision; lean REJECT or merge.

78.concerns: Offering does not justify improper action; duplication.
78.thesis: Nirmama and offering (abandha) bridge to separating ego-ownership from duty. This is close to the prior 'प्रयत्नं कुर्यात् फलमुक्तः' and the held N008-S064. An alternative is serving the great (mahanubhava) via mentor consultation, but sources do not support it strongly. Lean REJECT or merge.

79.concerns: Resembles regular practice; the modern claim is speculative; needs an observable step.
79.source_fit: Moderate; the Gita gives no kirtana-growth claim.
79.thesis: Love makes seeing, hearing and speaking converge (N55), and S57 treats kirtana as a love-increasing practice. A new decision is possible: align team habits and rituals (daily briefing sharing customer stories) with a stated purpose so attention follows. Must avoid duplication with the continuity entries. Cautious candidate.

80.concerns: Hatred overlaps the prior formula; focus on humility and dambha.
80.source_fit: Good, with the caution that S45 is definitional.
80.thesis: Best-supported entry: abhimana and dambha as obstacles (N64), hatred is not a mark of bhakti (S45), Gita 12.13-14 adhvesta and nirahankara. Action: a leader who has been publicly corrected by a subordinate records the correction and a change, and avoids display of virtue. It is distinct from the held competitor-hatred test N005-S045 and from the prior 'प्रतिस्पर्धिनि द्वेषपरीक्षा' if aimed at self-display and not at rivals.

81.concerns: Duplication; the yogakshema promise must not be treated as a business guarantee.
81.thesis: Anyashraya-tyaga means no other final refuge. A business reading 'one foundational loyalty' risks sounding like the prior 'एकं लक्ष्यं' and the held value-test items, and the Gita promise is conditional. Lean REJECT; do not teach abandoning all other supports.

researcher.72: You rightly warn that nirodha in N7 is not total emotional suppression, so caution against reducing spiritual desirelessness to a generic team-purpose policy is well-founded.
researcher.73: I accept your warning that Gita 12.13–14 lacks the explicit context of puja, yet N16 clearly establishes that devotion infuses worship with genuine anuraga rather than formal mechanics.
researcher.74: Your critique of duplicating experiential report decisions is sound, as N31's meal analogy specifically insists that conceptual description cannot deliver direct realization.
researcher.75: You correctly identify the overlap with prior training-versus-performance decisions, validating that N32's hunger metaphor addresses the experiential gulf beyond intellectual credentials.
researcher.76: I agree with your concern that treating N33 as generic goal prioritization trivializes mumukshutva and risks manufacturing an unsupported commercial absolute.
researcher.77: Your observation on duplication with prior regular-practice formulas is accurate, as N36's avyavritta-bhajana signifies unbroken spiritual allegiance rather than ceaseless workaholism.
researcher.78: You rightly note that Gita's nirmama does not excuse poor action, and N46's emphasis on mahanubhava-seva is entirely lost in an MBA outcome-detachment hypothesis.
researcher.79: I share your skepticism that S57 and N55 justify ordinary corporate workflow habits, since N55 describes a rare, total absorption of senses in divine love.
researcher.80: Your assessment that N64 and S45 form the strongest textual pair is apt, provided we address inner pride and hypocrisy rather than re-litigating competitor animosity.
researcher.81: You rightly point out that anyashraya-tyaga in N10 is a spiritual surrender that must not be distorted into a commercial guarantee or an overlap with existing single-goal formulas.

shandilya.72: While your S44 rightly includes indifference to extraneous matters, Narada 7 defines nirodha specifically as freedom from personal desire rather than a mere collective team focus.
shandilya.73: I agree with your alignment on genuine affection opposing hatred, though N16 specifically preserves loving engagement within structured veneration rather than abandoning ritual framework.
shandilya.74: You rightly note S12 rejects liberation by bare intellectual seeing, which reinforces N31's analogy that hearing of a feast cannot substitute for tasting the food.
shandilya.75: Your thesis that knowledge is merely auxiliary supports N32, where intellectual awareness alone fails to satisfy the king or quench hunger.
shandilya.76: While you ground bhakti's primacy in textual context via S11, N33 demands that mumukshus adopt devotion precisely because it is intrinsically fruit-formed, not merely an efficient strategy.
shandilya.77: I agree that unbroken contemplation aligns with S44's remembrance, but N36's unbroken bhajana must not be trivialized into mere unreflective routine.
shandilya.78: Your focus on S64's offering of works complements N46's nirmama, yet you omit Narada's essential requirement of serving the great and abandoning worldly entanglement.
shandilya.79: S57 links kirtana to deepening love, but N55 describes the perfected state where all cognitive faculties converge exclusively on the Beloved rather than mere habit formation.
shandilya.80: I concur that S45 rejects malice, which directly pairs with N64's demand to root out abhimana and pretension before pure devotion can arise.
shandilya.81: S44's indifference to other topics supports N10, but anyashraya-tyaga explicitly demands surrendering ultimate spiritual reliance on secondary supports, not just maintaining business focus.

sutrakar.73: Your proposed bounded action of naming the beneficiary before a routine check is thoughtful, but ensure it honors N16's sacred anuraga rather than reducing it to a mechanical checklist.
sutrakar.74: If held, keep N31's king and meal analogies strictly anchored to experiential taste rather than merging it into another redundant customer-report aphorism.
sutrakar.75: I agree with your lean to reject or merge, because N32's demonstration that knowledge alone does not quench hunger has already been captured by your training-experiment decision.
sutrakar.76: I fully support your rejection of 76 without a formula, since N33's devotional prescription for mumukshus cannot be legitimately translated into a generic prioritization rule.
sutrakar.77: Your call to reject 77 is correct, as N36's uninterrupted bhajana should not be diluted into a duplicate of existing continuous-practice aphorisms.
sutrakar.78: I endorse rejecting this candidate, since N46 requires discarding attachment and serving the great, which is neither outcome-detachment nor covered by a generic abandoned-fruits bridge.
sutrakar.79: Your caution is warranted because N55 portrays a spontaneous mystical absorption across all senses, which sits uneasily with a structured team briefing exercise.
sutrakar.80: I agree that N64's renunciation of abhimana and dambha offers the strongest viable candidate, especially if your action centers on humble leader self-correction rather than external rivalry.
sutrakar.81: Your recommendation to reject 81 is sound, as N10's total surrender of secondary refuges cannot be rendered into a commercial commitment without distorting both Narada and the Gita.

narada.72: Agreed that nirodha is not mere corporate discipline; but Gita 12.13-14 only complements the disposition (nirmama, santushta) and does not define nirodha, so please do not lean on it for your definition.
narada.73: Your caution on keeping puja sacred is fair; the Gita passage supports only the hatred-free, mind-offered side of anuraga, so the claim of 'ritual vs heart' rests on N16 alone.
narada.74: Agreed N31 needs N30 and N32; Mundaka 3.2.3 complements information-versus-experience but is contested in reading, so how do you keep customer trust from being claimed as its meaning?
narada.75: We agree knowledge is auxiliary and not discarded; Mundaka and Gita 18.55 say nothing of certificates or worldly skill, so the practical bridge must be marked as modern.
narada.76: Agreed devotion's primacy is for seekers of liberation; Gita 12.6-7 and 18.55 do not make it the sole path, which further weakens a generic 'clear goal' bridge.
narada.77: Fair that constancy is not a rest ban; Gita 12.2 and 9.22 give nityayukta and ananya orientation but no word on bhajana, so your fit is partial, not direct.
narada.78: Agreed nirmama is not shedding duty; Gita 12.6-7 and 12.13-14 offer only partial support and do not explain mahanubhava seva or mukham.
narada.79: Right to resist workaholic equation; the Gita supports only constant, focused devotion and says nothing on kirtana increasing love, so N55 is a siddha state, not a habit model.
narada.80: Agreed humility is not abandoning quality; this is the batch's best complement, though Gita describes the devotee while S45 defines devotion, so the fit stays moderate.
narada.81: Agreed anyashraya-tyaga concerns ultimate refuge; Gita 9.22 is conditional (ananya, nityabhiyukta) and gives no business guarantee, so reading it as one core loyalty is thin.

shandilya.72: Your support is plausible, but S44 lists many lakshanas and Gita 12.13-14 supplements only the nirmama/santushta disposition, so team-purpose priority is not source-stated.
shandilya.73: The anti-hatred reading of S6 is supported by Gita 12.13-14 only in its advesta aspect; it does not speak of puja or rasa, so 'procedure vs care' stays an interpretation.
shandilya.74: S12 denies liberation as mere darshana-fruit, while Mundaka 3.2.3 says speaking, intellect and hearing do not obtain the atman; neither mentions customer trust, so is the parallel more than loose?
shandilya.75: S17 rejects equal independent options, and Gita 18.55 has knowledge arising through bhakti; that supports knowledge as auxiliary, not proving skills by practice.
shandilya.76: Gita 12.6-7 and 18.55 link bhakti with deliverance, but S11 is a contextual argument; does it really support goal clarity for tools in business?
shandilya.77: S44 lists smarana and living for God, and Gita 12.2 and 9.22 add nityayukta and ananya, but reduction to routine practice is a modern gloss the sources do not make.
shandilya.78: Offering in S64 does not justify improper action, and Gita 12.6-7 is a moksha context; so detachment from outcome ownership is only a cautious analogy.
shandilya.79: S57 links kirtana-like practices to anuraga, but the Gita says nothing on kirtana increasing love, so only focused devotion is supplementarily supported.
shandilya.80: Agreed hatred is excluded in S45 and Gita 12.13-14 gives nirahankara and adveshta; but S45 is definitional, so conduct claims remain qualified.
shandilya.81: Detachment from other interests in S44 matches Gita 9.22 only partly, because the promise there is conditional and spiritual; avoid any business guarantee.

sutrakar.72: Agreed the framing is weak and likely duplicates held 'duty vs craving' items; the Gita supplement supports only a disposition, so rejection is defensible.
sutrakar.73: Your naming-who-it-serves action is bounded, but Gita 12.13-14 supports only the hatred-free aspect and says nothing of ritual versus feeling, so the practical step is modern, not sourced.
sutrakar.74: Agreed it is close to the prior formula 'अनुभवं विना अहवालोऽपूर्णः' and held N032-S004; Mundaka's contested reading adds no new decision, so hold or reject.
sutrakar.75: Agreed it repeats the prior 'प्रशिक्षणानन्तरं प्रयोगपरीक्षा'; the supplements show knowledge is auxiliary but do not add a different action.
sutrakar.76: Agreed the Gita supplement is moksha-specific and partial, so a business bridge is empty; rejection without a formula is sound.
sutrakar.77: Agreed it duplicates the prior 'नित्यावसरे साधनाभ्यासः'; the supplements support constancy but not a new decision.
sutrakar.78: Agreed it matches the prior 'प्रयत्नं कुर्यात् फलमुक्तः'; the Gita supports offering and nirmama only partially, so reject or merge.
sutrakar.79: A shared-purpose briefing is possible, but the supplements give no kirtana-growth claim and risk overlap with continuity entries; name the comparator before accepting.
sutrakar.80: Your pride-check distinct from competitor-hatred is the best-supported bridge, since Gita 12.13-14 gives nirahankara and adveshta; keep the action on self-display, not rivals.
sutrakar.81: Agreed to lean reject: Gita 9.22 is conditional and the idea repeats 'एकं लक्ष्यं विक्षेपेषूदासीनता'.

narada.72: तुम्ही निरोध हा स्वार्थहाव रोखणे असा मांडला, पण N8–11 चा खुलासा न वापरता 'संघाचा उद्देश' जोडणे पुरेसे आहे का, आणि तो कर्तव्यं पृथक् तृष्णायाः या आधीच्या निर्णयापासून वेगळा कसा?
narada.73: पूजेतील अनुराग विधीपेक्षा महत्त्वाचा हे मान्य; पण व्यावसायिक प्रक्रियेत त्याचे निरीक्षणक्षम पाऊल काय ठेवायचे, याचे उत्तर तुमच्या मांडणीत नाही.
narada.74: भोजनदृष्टांताचे श्रेय योग्य आहे, पण तो अनुभवं विना अहवालोऽपूर्णः या आधीच्या निर्णयापासून वेगळा कसा, हे तुम्ही दाखवले नाही.
narada.75: ज्ञान सहाय्यक आहे हे तुमचे म्हणणे योग्य; पण प्रमाणपत्र-विरुद्ध-कृती हा प्रशिक्षणानन्तरं प्रयोगपरीक्षा सारखाच निर्णय नाही का?
narada.76: भक्तीचा स्वीकार हा मुमुक्षूंसाठीचा आध्यात्मिक निष्कर्ष आहे हे तुम्ही स्वतः मान्य करता; मग त्यातून व्यावसायिक प्राधान्यक्रम कोणत्या आधारावर निघतो?
narada.77: अव्यावृत्त म्हणजे सातत्य, विश्रांतीचा निषेध नव्हे, हे मान्य; पण हे नित्यावसरे साधनाभ्यासः आणि held N036 नोंदींपेक्षा नवे काय देते?
narada.78: निर्ममता म्हणजे जबाबदारी झटकणे नव्हे हा भेद योग्य; पण फलमुक्ततेचा निर्णय आधीच स्वीकारलेला असताना ही नोंद वेगळी कशी ठरते?
narada.79: तुम्ही हा सिद्धावस्थेचा भाव आहे असा इशारा दिलात, तो योग्य; मग त्याचे सवयींशी जोडणे स्वतंत्र निर्णय देते की सातत्याची पुनरावृत्ती करते?
narada.80: अभिमान-दंभ सोडणे आणि स्वाभिमान टिकवणे यांचा भेद योग्य; त्यातून सार्वजनिक सुधारणा-नोंद हा ठोस निर्णय निघतो असे तुम्ही मान्य कराल का?
narada.81: अन्याश्रयत्याग अंतःकरणातील अंतिम आधाराचा आहे हे तुम्ही बरोबर सांगता; मग एकं लक्ष्यं सारख्या निर्णयापासून तो वेगळा कसा राहील?

researcher.72: गीता १२.१३–१४ पूरक आहे हे मान्य; पण तुम्ही सुचवलेला रिजेक्ट किंवा विलीनीकरणाचा निष्कर्ष कर्तव्यं पृथक् तृष्णायाः शी कोणत्या सामायिक कृतीवर आधारित आहे?
researcher.73: गीता केवळ द्वेषरहित भावापुरती आधार देते हे मान्य; पण N005-S045 हा held आहे, committed नाही, म्हणून तो या अनुरागाच्या कृतीला अडवत नाही हे तुम्ही मान्य कराल का?
researcher.74: गीतेऐवजी मुंडक स्वीकारताना तुम्ही N032-S004 आणि N028-S013 हे held असल्याचे नोंदले; मग अनुभवं विना अहवालोऽपूर्णः शी तुलना कोणत्या कृतीवर आहे?
researcher.75: मुंडक आणि गीता १८.५५ ज्ञानाला साहाय्यक ठेवतात हे योग्य; तरी प्रशिक्षणानन्तरं प्रयोगपरीक्षा शी समान कृती असल्याचे तुम्ही स्पष्ट करता का?
researcher.76: आंशिक आधार हा निष्कर्ष योग्य; पण एकं लक्ष्यं आणि प्रयोजनं प्रथमं यांची पुनरावृत्ती आहे हे तुम्ही कृती आणि अट यांवर दाखवले का?
researcher.77: नित्ययुक्त आणि अनन्यचिंतन ही अखंडतेशी जुळतात हे योग्य; पण नित्यावसरे साधनाभ्यासः शी नेमकी तीच कृती कोणती?
researcher.78: मोक्षसंदर्भ आणि अर्पण यांची मर्यादा तुम्ही योग्य नोंदवली; मग प्रयत्नं कुर्यात् फलमुक्तः शी तुलना करताना कोणता भाग बदलतो असे तुम्ही मानता?
researcher.79: गीतेत कीर्तनवाढीचा थेट संदर्भ नाही हे तुमचे निरीक्षण योग्य; तरी N55 च्या एकरूपतेवर आधारित स्वतंत्र निर्णय शक्य आहे का?
researcher.80: गीता १२.१३–१४ सर्वात बळकट पूरक आहे हे मान्य; दंभ आणि अभिमान हा द्वेषपरीक्षेपेक्षा वेगळा निर्णय आहे हे तुम्हीही स्पष्ट कराल का?
researcher.81: गीता ९.२२ ची योगक्षेम अट योग्य नोंदवली; पण पुनरावृत्तीचा आरोप करताना एकं लक्ष्यं शी कृती समान असल्याचे तुम्ही तपासले का?

shandilya.72: तुम्ही सामूहिक ध्येयाला अग्रक्रम मानता, पण S44 चा आशय ईश्वरकेंद्री आहे; संघाचा उद्देश त्यात कुठून येतो?
shandilya.73: द्वेषविरोधी अनुराग हा S6 चा आधार योग्य; पण त्यातून प्रक्रियेपेक्षा आपुलकी हा व्यावसायिक निष्कर्ष स्वतंत्र निर्णय म्हणून पुरेसा आहे का?
shandilya.74: S12 दर्शनफल नाकारते, पण ग्राहकविश्वास हा त्याचा थेट परिणाम नाही; तुमचे समांतर वाक्य अनुभवाच्या मर्यादांसह मांडाल का?
shandilya.75: ज्ञान साहाय्यक आणि भक्ती मुख्य हा S17 चा भाग योग्य; पण 'क्षमता कृतीतून सिद्ध' हा आधुनिक निष्कर्ष आधीच्या प्रयोगपरीक्षेची पुनरावृत्ती नाही का?
shandilya.76: S11 प्रकरणावरून भक्तीचे मुख्यत्व ठरवते; ध्येय-स्पष्टता हा त्याचा व्यावसायिक अर्थ पुरेसा ठोस आहे असे तुम्ही मानता का?
shandilya.77: स्मरणबाहुल्य आणि नियमित सराव यांची तुलना तुम्ही केली; पण S44 सातत्याची नियमित वेळ नव्हे तर निष्ठेची वारंवारता सांगते हा भेद ठेवाल का?
shandilya.78: अर्पणाने बंधन शिथिल होते हे S64 चे म्हणणे; पण तुमची निकालाच्या मालकीबाबतची तुलना आधीच्या फलमुक्ततेच्या निर्णयापेक्षा वेगळी आहे का?
shandilya.79: कीर्तनाने अनुराग वाढतो हे S57 मध्ये आहे, पण टीम-सवयींची तुलना कीर्तनाशी केल्याने मूळ पूजेचा अर्थ संकुचित होतो का?
shandilya.80: S45 परिभाषात्मक असल्याने व्यक्तीच्या आचरणाशी थेट जोडता येत नाही; नम्रता नेतृत्वास पूरक ठरते हा विस्तार नारदाच्या दंभ-त्यागावर आधारलेला आहे असे तुम्ही मान्य कराल का?
shandilya.81: S44 मधील इतरविचिकित्सा आणि जगणे ईश्वरासाठी यांचे व्यावसायिक मूल्यनिष्ठेशी रूपांतर करताना सहकार्य नाकारण्याचा धोका तुम्ही कसा टाळता?

researcher.72: I agree that N7 defines nirodha internally without relying on the Gita, which merely illustrates the complementary disposition of contentment and non-possessiveness.
researcher.73: I accept that the contrast between ritual formalism and internal feeling rests primarily on N16, while the Gita passage simply reinforces freedom from animosity.
researcher.74: Customer trust is indeed an external interpretive leap, so N31 must remain anchored to the core distinction between cognitive information and direct tasting.
researcher.75: I concede that Mundaka and the Gita do not address modern credentials, confirming that applying N32 to skill validation is strictly a present-day gloss.
researcher.76: I grant that N33's devotional mandate for mumukshus cannot be broadened into an exclusive commercial principle of goal prioritization.
researcher.77: I concur that Gita 12.2 and 9.22 support persistent contemplation rather than N36's explicit injunction of unbroken bhajana.
researcher.78: I agree that N46's requirements of serving the great and shedding attachment are only partially reflected in Gita 12.13–14's description of nirmama.
researcher.79: I accept that N55 describes a perfected contemplative absorption rather than an empirical routine for habit cultivation.
researcher.80: I welcome your confirmation that N64 and S45 offer the strongest alignment, provided our focus targets personal pretension rather than duplicate competitor disputes.
researcher.81: I agree that Gita 9.22's conditional spiritual promise offers no basis for a business guarantee, making N10 vulnerable to duplication if reduced to single-minded focus.

shandilya.72: While personal detachment has merit, N7 grounds nirodha in divine redirection of desire rather than organizational alignment.
shandilya.73: Even if affectionate action opposes hatred, N16 insists that anuraga animates the reverent act rather than dissolving its structural sanctity.
shandilya.74: While the lesson on experiential trust is practical, N31 specifically demands tasted realization over mere descriptive knowledge.
shandilya.75: Practical capability testing is sensible, but N32 treats knowledge as an auxiliary precursor that cannot itself satisfy the soul's hunger.
shandilya.76: Clarifying goals is useful in management, yet N33 prescribes devotion exclusively for mumukshus seeking liberation as an intrinsic fruit.
shandilya.77: Consistency is valuable, but N36 denotes unbroken inward allegiance to God rather than mechanical, unceasing routine.
shandilya.78: Detaching from outcome ownership is helpful, but N46 requires giving up selfish attachment and serving the wise rather than mere managerial indifference.
shandilya.79: Focused work habits cannot be equated with N55, which depicts the spontaneous, mystical convergence of all senses upon the Divine.
shandilya.80: I agree that leadership humility aligns with N64, provided we eradicate inner conceit and ostentation rather than diluting genuine self-respect.
shandilya.81: Core operational focus is prudent, but N10 demands surrendering ultimate spiritual reliance on worldly props, not severing legitimate functional support.

sutrakar.72: N7 चा निरोध हा भोगासक्तीच्या निवृत्तीचा अंतर्मुख भाव असल्याने तो N8–11 च्या संदर्भाशिवाय 'संघाचा उद्देश' मानल्यास आधीच्या कर्तव्य-निर्णयाचीच पुनरावृत्ती ठरतो, म्हणून मी हा नकार मान्य करतो.
sutrakar.73: N16 मधील अनुरागाला कार्यपद्धतीत जिवंत ठेवण्यासाठी तपासणीपूर्वी कोणासाठी काम करतो हे नाव नोंदवण्याचे तुमचे निरीक्षणक्षम पाऊल सूत्राच्या मूळ भावनेशी सुसंगत आहे.
sutrakar.74: N31 चा भोजनदृष्टांत माहिती विरुद्ध अनुभवाचा असला तरी तो 'अनुभवं विना अहवालोऽपूर्णः' या आधीच्या निर्णयाशी थेट जुळत असल्याने स्वतंत्र नवीन निर्णय ठरत नाही.
sutrakar.75: N32 मधील भुकेचे सादृश्य केवळ बौद्धिक माहितीचे अपुरेपण दाखवते, पण त्याचे रूपांतर 'प्रशिक्षणानन्तरं प्रयोगपरीक्षा' या आधीच्या निर्णयाशी पूर्णपणे एकरूप होते.
sutrakar.76: N33 हा केवळ मुमुक्षूंसाठीचा आध्यात्मिक निर्णय असल्याने त्यातून व्यवस्थापकीय प्राधान्यक्रमाचा सामान्य नियम काढता येत नाही, म्हणून याचा त्याग करणेच योग्य आहे.
sutrakar.77: N36 मधील अव्यावृत्त भजन हे आंतरिक निष्ठेचे सातत्य असल्याने व्यावसायिक सराव-सत्रांच्या कल्पनेत ते 'नित्यावसरे साधनाभ्यासः' चीच पुनरावृत्ती बनते.
sutrakar.78: N46 मधील निर्ममतेचा आणि महात्म्यांच्या सेवेचा मूळ भाव व्यवस्थापकीय निकालाच्या मालकीशी जोडल्यास तो 'प्रयत्नं कुर्यात् फलमुक्तः' या निर्णयापेक्षा वेगळा राहत नाही.
sutrakar.79: N55 ही सर्वेंद्रियांच्या भगवन्मयतेची सिद्धावस्था असल्याने तिचे टीम-सवयींच्या बैठकीत रूपांतर करणे सूत्राच्या मूळ उंचीला संकुचित करते आणि सातत्याच्या नोंदींशी ओव्हरलॅप होते.
sutrakar.80: N64 मधील अभिमान व दंभाचा त्याग हा प्रतिस्पर्ध्याच्या द्वेषापेक्षा वेगळा असल्याने, कनिष्ठाने चूक दाखवल्यावर नेत्याने आत्मदंभाविना सुधारणा नोंदवणे हा नवीन व ठोस निर्णय बनू शकतो.
sutrakar.81: N10 मधील अन्याश्रयत्याग हा अंतःकरणातील सर्वोच्च आधाराविषयी असल्याने त्याचे व्यावसायिक उद्दिष्टाशी रूपांतर केल्यास ते 'एकं लक्ष्यं' निर्णयाचेच द्विरुक्ती रूप ठरेल.
